note: Figures are planning estimates for October 2026. Confirm costs with suppliers and official portals before you commit money. Shares of startup budget must add up to 1.

blueprints.name: POS Agent Business
licences: CAC business name (₦10,500 official fees, verify on cac.gov.ng)
Partnership with a CBN-licensed payment service provider or bank
Location and signage (no special licence for most states)

startupBreakdown.item: Power backup (inverter or small generator running cost)

profitTimeline.label: Setting up, testing float flow, building neighbourhood trust
Break-even on fixed costs if you hit about 150 transactions a day
Steady profit if you have a second float source and clean records

steps: Pick a busy spot with heavy foot traffic: a bus stop, market entrance, or near a school.
Register a business name with CAC (sole proprietorship) and open a business bank account.
Apply through a licensed payment service provider or bank partner as an agent.
Start with a small float, then grow it after you prove your daily turnover.
Keep a daily ledger: opening float, transactions, closing float, and cash count.
Build repeat customers with fast service, clean receipts, and a predictable schedule.
failurePoints: Float runs out at peak hours

suppliers.name: Licensed PSP or bank partner
suppliers.where: Apply online or at a branch
suppliers.note: Ask for written terms and commission schedule. Never pay a 'joining fee' in cash to a stranger.

blueprints.spark: Set up at a school gate or market entrance where people need quick transfers. Your first 50 customers come from people you already know.
blueprints.premiumNotes: Premium: a 90-day float plan, daily ledger template, and the three-question checklist before you sign any agent agreement.

blueprints.name: Mini Provision Store
licences: LGA trading or shop permit (varies by council)

startupBreakdown.item: Opening stock (rice, sugar, drinks, noodles, toiletries)

profitTimeline.label: Learning your fast sellers and slow sellers
Break-even on rent and power once daily sales are stable
Real profit if you cut credit and manage stock turnover

steps: Survey 20 households near the shop and list what they buy every week.
Register the business and get a TIN for the business.
Buy opening stock from a wholesale market (Mile 12, Idumota, Ariaria, or Kantin Kwari depending on your city).
Set up a simple cash book and a 'do not sell on credit' rule for the first 90 days.
Rotate stock and track expiry dates. Expired goods are pure loss.
Add jara and loyalty for your best customers.
failurePoints: Buying what you like instead of what sells
No power backup for fridge items

suppliers.name: Wholesale clusters
suppliers.where: Mile 12 (Lagos), Idumota (Lagos), Ariaria (Aba), Onitsha Main Market, Kantin Kwari (Kano)
suppliers.note: Go early, bring cash, and buy from registered distributors where possible.

blueprints.spark: Sell small packs of sugar, Indomie and pure water at the bus stop before 8am. Early hours can pay the rent.
blueprints.premiumNotes: Premium: a 12-month stock calendar, a sample product list with margin targets, and a credit policy template.

blueprints.name: Suya Spot (Grill Business)
licences: Food vendor permit or LGA approval
Food handler health checks (state rules vary)

startupBreakdown.item: First stock of beef and spices
Gas or charcoal and cooking fuel

profitTimeline.label: Finding your spice mix and daily meat cost
Regular night crowd, break-even on fixed costs
December and festive seasons can double sales

steps: Pick a night spot with heavy foot traffic and parking, near a hostel, campus or office block.
Test your spice mix on 30 friends and track feedback.
Buy meat fresh each morning and track weight loss on the grill.
Register the business and get the local permit needed.
Use a fixed price per stick and per pack so you can plan your cost.
Build a WhatsApp order list for pre-orders and the festive season.
failurePoints: Burnt or dry suya killing reviews

suppliers.name: Cattle and meat sourcing
suppliers.where: Local abattoirs and meat wholesalers. Kantin Kwari or Sabon Gari for spices in Kano; markets in Lagos for pepper and spice
suppliers.note: Buy in bulk when prices dip. Keep your supplier relationship consistent.

blueprints.spark: Sell suya packs with a fixed price and a WhatsApp pre-order for weekends. You control the stock and the crowd.
blueprints.premiumNotes: Premium: a spice-mix costing sheet, daily meat ordering plan, and a festive season calendar.

blueprints.name: Thrift Fashion Business
licences: Business name (optional at start, needed for bank and bigger sellers)

profitTimeline.label: Learning which bales sell and which pile up
Break-even when your sales are consistent every week
Profit if you build repeat buyers and a clear return policy

steps: Buy a small bale first from a trusted seller and grade the content before you sell.
Sort into categories: denim, jackets, dresses, shoes, and accessories.
Clean, steam and photograph every piece in good light.
Post daily on Instagram and TikTok, and sell through WhatsApp Status.
Set a clear return and refund policy to build trust.
Reinvest the first profit into the best-selling category.
failurePoints: Bales with too many damaged pieces

suppliers.name: Bale markets
suppliers.where: Ikeja and Lagos Island bale markets; Aba and Onitsha for local fabrics and factory overruns
suppliers.note: Compare the same bale at two sellers before you pay.

blueprints.spark: Post one bale-opening video a week. People buy the story as much as the clothes.
blueprints.premiumNotes: Premium: a bale grading checklist, a WhatsApp catalogue template and a 60-day content calendar.

blueprints.name: Phone Accessories Shop
licences: Warranty and returns policy for resold goods

profitTimeline.label: Learning fast-moving accessories and supplier prices
Break-even when you sell about 40 small items a day
Repair add-on and screen protectors boost margins

steps: Pick a shop in a dense phone area like Computer Village (Ikeja), Idumota or a busy campus.
Buy from two or three suppliers and test every item before you stock it.
Register the business and get your display space.
Sell genuine accessories with a clear warranty.
Add screen protector fitting or phone repair as a side service.
Track fast and slow lines each week.

suppliers.name: Electronics clusters
suppliers.where: Computer Village (Ikeja), Idumota (Lagos Island), Onitsha electronics area, and Ogbete market (Enugu)
suppliers.note: Ask for samples. Never buy a 'bulk offer' without testing.

blueprints.spark: Offer free screen-protector fitting when someone buys a case. Your repeat customers come from small service wins.
blueprints.premiumNotes: Premium: a fake-detection checklist for chargers and earphones, and a 6-month product mix plan.

blueprints.name: Laundry and Cleaning Service
licences: Waste disposal arrangement with the LGA

startupBreakdown.item: Washing machine and dryer (or manual setup)

profitTimeline.label: Finding your pickup routes and pricing
Break-even once you have regular hostel or office clients
Profit once you have contracts with offices or estates

steps: Choose a service area with students, apartments or offices nearby.
Price per item and per kg, and publish both.
Set up a pickup and delivery schedule.
Get the power plan right before you buy machines.
Register the business and open a business account.
Ask for monthly contracts from offices and landlords.

suppliers.name: Machine and detergent suppliers
suppliers.where: Local dealers in the nearest industrial area or market
suppliers.note: Ask for warranty and after-sales service in writing.

blueprints.spark: Offer a monthly subscription for students in one hostel. Predictable money beats one-off jobs.
blueprints.premiumNotes: Premium: a power cost model (inverter vs generator), a price sheet template and a client onboarding script.

blueprints.name: Generator Servicing and Sales
licences: Environmental and safety compliance for fuel storage

startupBreakdown.item: Spare parts starter stock (filters, plugs, oil)

profitTimeline.label: Building a client list in estates and offices
Break-even on van and rent
Service contracts keep the cash flowing

steps: Get trained on the most common generator brands in your area.
Register the business and set up a simple invoice template.
Build a parts list for the top 10 faults.
Offer servicing packages to estates, offices and shops.
Sell pre-owned or new units with a warranty.
Track every job so you can quote accurately.

suppliers.name: Parts and generator markets
suppliers.where: Lagos (Ikeja, Mile 2), Onitsha, Kano, and Port Harcourt generator and spares markets
suppliers.note: Buy genuine parts where possible. Fakes damage your reputation fast.

blueprints.spark: Offer a quarterly servicing plan to 10 offices. Recurring work pays better than one-off repairs.
blueprints.premiumNotes: Premium: a fault-diagnosis checklist, a service contract template and a 12-month parts plan.

blueprints.name: Home Baking and Chin Chin Business
licences: NAFDAC registration for packaged food sold to the public (required for commercial sale of processed foods)

profitTimeline.label: Recipe testing and price setting
Repeat orders on WhatsApp
Festive season and office orders drive the big money

steps: Test recipes on 20 people and keep a feedback log.
Cost each product per unit, including packaging and delivery.
Register the business name with CAC.
For sold packaged food, check NAFDAC requirements before you sell beyond friends and family.
Build a WhatsApp catalogue with pre-order slots.
Offer bulk packs for offices, churches and owambe events.

suppliers.name: Ingredient and packaging sourcing
suppliers.where: Mile 12 (Lagos), Ariaria (Aba), Kantin Kwari (Kano) for bulk ingredients; packaging from local dealers
suppliers.note: Buy consistent brands so your product tastes the same every batch.

blueprints.spark: Sell a chin chin tin for office workers on Friday. Friday pre-orders are where most food side-hustles start.
blueprints.premiumNotes: Premium: a NAFDAC checklist, a per-unit costing sheet and a festive order calendar.

lagos.label: Lagos
lagos.note: High rent, fast customers, fierce competition.

onitsha.label: Onitsha
onitsha.note: Strong wholesale, cheaper stock, strong trading culture.

kano.label: Kano
kano.note: Lower capital needs, grain and textile strength.

aba.label: Aba
aba.note: Factory-direct fashion and shoes, strong local demand.

abuja.label: Abuja
abuja.note: Higher incomes and rent, good for premium services.

port-harcourt.label: Port Harcourt
port-harcourt.note: Generator and power costs are high. Good for backup services.

enugu.label: Enugu
enugu.note: Affordable rent and a strong trading base.

kaduna.label: Kaduna
kaduna.note: Lower costs, strong grain and textile trade.

benin-city.label: Benin City
benin-city.note: Good food supply and a growing trading base.
